data.goal: Fix the requests Session so that environment variables REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE and CURL_CA_BUNDLE are ignored when self.verify is explicitly set to False, by resolving None verify kwargs against self.verify before checking environment CA bundles.

edit_targets.expected_behavior_change: When the verify kwarg is None, resolve it to self.verify before deciding whether to override it with the REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE or CURL_CA_BUNDLE environment variables so that session.verify = False is respected.

implementation_steps: Step 1: In src/requests/sessions.py, modify Session.merge_environment_settings. Immediately before the existing block that checks verify is True or verify is None against the environment CA bundles, add an assignment: if verify is None: verify = self.verify. This ensures the session-level verify setting is consulted before the environment override logic runs.

Step 2: In src/requests/sessions.py, update the existing environment CA bundle check inside merge_environment_settings to only apply env bundles when verify is True or None (keeping the existing condition, which now correctly skips application when verify is False or a string path).

Step 3: Add a unit test in tests/test_requests.py that creates a Session with verify=False, sets the REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE environment variable to an invalid path, and asserts that making a request does not raise an exception related to the invalid CA bundle path.
risks: There is a small risk that downstream code relies on the current behavior where a session with verify=None (default) and REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE set would still apply the env bundle even if session.verify were later mutated to False, though this is exactly the bug being fixed.
